When did it start?
It started on my right hand three weeks ago.
I did not change anything that week.
The cream made it worse and two blisters appeared last Friday.
Tell me about the patches. When did they start?
The onset was about six weeks ago. Two patches on my elbows first, then one on my knee.
Did anything change in your life around that time?
I changed jobs in March and I did not sleep for about a month. Stress is my trigger, I think. It always was.
What do the patches look like? Are they scaly, or wet?
Dry and scaly. When I scratch them, small pieces come off. Last week the skin around one of them was swollen.
Did you use anything on them?
A cream my sister gave me. It did not help, and it burned. Is that a side effect, or did I make it worse?

I teach residents the same eight questions, in the same order, and the order is not decoration. The first one is always when did it start. Not how long have you had it, which invites a shrug, but when did it start, which asks for a date. And people remember. They say, it was the week I moved apartment, or it started the day after the wedding. That date organises everything that comes after it. The second question is where did it start, because the place it began is almost never the place it is worst now, and residents tend to examine the loudest patch and write that down as the origin. Then what does it look like, then what makes it worse. And here is the thing about what makes it worse: patients almost never volunteer a trigger. They do not think of it as information. So you have to ask directly, and you have to ask about the week before the onset, not about their habits in general. Did anything change that week. A new soap, a new tablet, a new job. The question residents forget most often is the last one, and it is the one I would keep if I could only keep one. What have you already put on it. Half of what I see on the skin was put there by the patient, before they came to me.

It burns now, that is the thing, it never burned before. Sorry, let me go back. It started in the spring, about two months ago, and it was one small dry patch behind my ear, nothing at all. I put moisturiser on it for a couple of weeks and it did nothing, so I stopped. Then my mother gave me a cream she had at home, an old one, and honestly for about four days it looked better. And then it stopped working, and after that I did not put anything on it for three weeks because I was afraid of making it worse. And in those three weeks it spread to my neck, which is when I called you. My sister says it is stress and maybe she is right, my job changed too. Oh. Now that I am saying all of this out loud, there is one more thing, and I almost forgot it because it has nothing to do with my skin. I started a new tablet for my blood pressure at the beginning of the spring. Right at the beginning. Is that the kind of thing you need to know?

When did it start, exactly? Where on the body did it start? What do the patches look like? Did anything change in the week before it started? Did you use anything on it? Did it help, or did it make it worse?
